quotes.text: Following Roth's departure, the band recruited Matthias Jabs and began moving towards a more melodic rock style on their sixth studio album Lovedrive (1979).

I am all fine with experimenting, but with such a drastic change, it is a little too much all at once. The techno sound, the rapping, the almost full album of ballads was too shocking for most humans to handle.

the Scorpions are not a boy band, they are not a pop band and they are definitely not a techno band. They are a hard rock, heavy metal giant that got lost in the 90's like a lot of 70's/80's bands did.
It is funny how some of the 80's bands went really heavy in the mid-90's and changed up their sound completely, Scorpions thought the softer route was the way to go…they were wrong.
'Lonesome Crow' is psychedelic ride that will leave you tripping, but also scratching your head as it is unfocused, experimental and not what you'd expect when you hear the band name Scorpions.
It is really more an instrumental, jam style record with a little Klaus thrown in so you don't forget he is there.

The idea of a heavier Scorpions would've been great, but they could find the right feel. The band seemed to be out of steam as they tried to be political due to the success of "Wind of Change", but that direction led them to lose themselves and what makes the Scorpions…the Scorpions.
They're a great, melodic hard rock band. The Scorpions have rarely been dour.
With a lead guitarist as skilled as Rudolf Schenker, you'd think they'd get more reverence from the hard rock faithful.
Klaus Meine was a charismatic front man and Matthias Jabs and the aforementioned Rudolf Schenker were a dynamic dual lead guitar threat.
It wasn't until I was in college that the Scorpions exploded with the metal masterpiece Blackout.
The Scorpions even dabbled in politics on Love At First Sting with the anti-war and at the time anti Cold War track "Crossfire."
The band said they've tried to produce a record more in line with their earlier work. There is a great mix of tempos and styles.

'Rock Believer' may not have the 'forks in your eyes' power of 'Blackout' or the 'titillation of your ears' given by 'Lovedrive', but, get your First Aid kits ready because this Scorpions album has got a sting.
